chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Eddie Heywood's band, its records and the John Kirby comparison
summary: He hated to see Heywood's good band break up, says records featured only Eddie, and contrasts it with John Kirby's intricate band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Eddie Heywood's band was quite popular for a while.
It was. It really was. It kind of brought me down for him to have to break up that band. You know, they were going so nicely. I hated to see it break up. It
was such a good band, you know?
Is it well represented on the records, do you think, or was...?

I don't think they got enough push on the records. There's only one or two records they pushed, and it didn't consist of the band. It just featured him, Eddie, you know, and people really didn't get to be exposed to the band like they should have. Like John Kirby's band, you could hear the band always. Such a beautiful... There was the only two little small bands, that was Eddie Heywood's and John Kirby's. And John Kirby's band was such a versatile band. Such beautiful playing.
Ours was a different type of band. Ours was a more like a Swing...like a Jump-Swing thing, you know. Theirs was more intricate things. They were so nice! So nice they made...
